reviews.source_title: Total DNS outage in Kubernetes cluster
reported_symptoms: Downstream calls timed out and application retries increased request volume.
CoreDNS memory usage spiked and all CoreDNS pods repeatedly OOMKilled.
Cluster DNS became unavailable and in-cluster monitoring also failed.
reviews.reported_root_cause: A retry-driven DNS query spike exhausted a very small CoreDNS memory limit, after which repeated OOM kills produced a cluster-wide DNS outage.
contributing_factors: The application did not cache DNS lookups.
Default ndots:5 behavior multiplied queries for external names.
Short-lived HTTP connections increased DNS lookup frequency.
CoreDNS had a 100Mi memory limit based on historical rather than spike usage.
Most monitoring depended on the same cluster DNS failure domain.
reported_mitigations: The incident team increased CoreDNS memory requests and limits to recover service.
The postmortem proposed more resilient node-local DNS and external alerting.
reusable_checks: Correlate DNS timeout growth with CoreDNS request rate, memory, restarts, and OOM termination reasons.
Inspect pod resolv.conf and ndots behavior before assuming the upstream DNS server is the only cause.
Check whether retries, connection-pool lifetime, or missing application DNS caching amplify query volume.
Verify that DNS and control-plane alerts have an out-of-cluster notification path.
Separate CoreDNS container-limit OOM from node-wide Linux memory pressure.
safe_commands: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns -o wide
risky_or_historical_actions: Do not copy the historical 2000Mi CoreDNS limit without measuring the current workload and cluster.
Do not deploy a new DNS architecture during an incident without compatibility, rollback, and blast-radius review.
applicability: The incident occurred in 2019 and its exact versions and DNS topology are historical.
The evidence pattern remains useful for CoreDNS OOM, retry storms, ndots amplification, and monitoring dependency failures.
Current Kubernetes DNS, NodeLocal DNSCache, runtime, and cloud-provider behavior must be verified.
source_notes: The source explicitly separates the outage timeline, contributing factors, lessons, and action items.
Reported facts are paraphrased; AOP does not copy the full postmortem.

reviews.source_title: Kubernetes Networking Problems Due to the Conntrack
reported_symptoms: A high-load aggregation service developed connectivity failures and elevated errors.
Affected nodes approached their conntrack entry limits.
reviews.reported_root_cause: Node conntrack tables became exhausted after node RAM was reduced while downstream sharding increased the number of tracked connections.
contributing_factors: The workload sustained high request volume with large connection fan-out.
Nodes were resized to half the previous RAM.
Downstream sharding doubled the connections that needed tracking.
reported_mitigations: The service was scheduled onto nodes with more RAM.
The number of aggregation pods per node was limited.
Conntrack utilization monitoring and alerting were added.
reusable_checks: Compare current conntrack entries with the configured maximum on each affected node.
Correlate resets and timeouts with node placement, request rate, connection fan-out, and recent node resizing.
Check conntrack insert failures and table-full kernel messages before changing limits.
Review pod density and connection-heavy workload concentration per node.
Treat conntrack tuning as a capacity and memory decision, not a universal fix.
risky_or_historical_actions: Do not copy a historical nf_conntrack_max value without measuring node memory and current kernel behavior.
Do not let arbitrary application init containers or competing DaemonSets mutate node conntrack sysctls.
Privileged sysctl mutation requires change control, rollback, and node-memory impact review.
applicability: The source describes GKE behavior observed in 2020 and references Kubernetes 1.15-era changes.
Current managed-cluster defaults, kernel counters, kube-proxy mode, CNI, and node sizing must be verified.
The evidence pattern remains useful for high connection fan-out, resets, intermittent timeouts, and node-local saturation.
source_notes: The source provides observed symptoms, conntrack metrics, immediate mitigation, and explicit cautions about sysctl mutation.
Reported facts are paraphrased; AOP does not copy the full article.
